issues.description: The problem statement specifies the method addRating(stars:) should take a parameter of type Double, but both the template and the solution declare addRating(stars:) with parameter type Int. This mismatch between the described parameter type and the code signatures will confuse students about what type to use and will prevent them from matching the provided template/solution (and likely the tests).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the parameter type consistent across all artifacts. Preferred minimal fix: update the problem statement to require addRating(stars:) to accept an Int (1–5) to match the template and solution. Alternatively, if you intend to use Double ratings, update the template and solution to accept Double and change the ratings array to [Double], updating average calculations accordingly.

issues.description: Within the problem statement there is an internal type inconsistency: the ratings property is described as an array of Int, but the addRating(stars:) method is described to take a Double. This contradicts the property type described for ratings and creates ambiguity about whether ratings should store Ints or Doubles.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the rating element type consistent in the problem statement and code. Either: (A) change the problem text to state that ratings are Int values and addRating accepts an Int; or (B) change the ratings property in the template/solution to [Double] and have addRating accept Double, adjusting average calculation to use Double sums. Option A is the smaller change and aligns with the existing template/solution.
